**Role and context anchoring** improves compliance. Assigning personas ("You are a compliance officer") and establishing behavioral expectations shapes how models interpret and execute tasks.

# Journal Procedure

`journal.md` at the repository root is the append-only institutional memory of this project. It exists so no failure is ever retried blindly and no work is ever redone.

## Reading (start of every session)

Read the last 20 entries in full, plus the TL;DR line of every older entry. If an older TL;DR looks relevant to your task, read that entry in full too. Your first entry of the session notes which past entries were relevant.

## Writing

Append an entry after every meaningful unit of work: a file edited, a test run, a decision made, an approach abandoned. Do not batch a session into one entry at the end. Rules:

- Append-only. Correct a wrong past entry with a new entry that references the old one by timestamp; never edit or delete history.
- Absolute timestamps, never "today" or "earlier".
- Reference code as `path:line`.
- Quote error messages and test output verbatim.

## Entry template

```markdown
## [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] — <short title of the work unit>

**TL;DR:** One or two sentences: what was done and the outcome.

**Long description:** Full narrative — what was attempted, exact files and
functions touched, reasoning behind the approach, commands run, relevant
output or errors quoted verbatim.

**What worked:** Concrete successes, with evidence (test output, observed behavior).

**What failed:** Every approach tried that did not work, why, and the exact
error messages. This section exists so failures are never retried blindly.

**What was kept / discarded:** Which changes survived, which were reverted or
deleted, and why.

**Open questions / next steps:** Anything unresolved or deferred, stated
precisely enough that a future agent can pick it up cold.
```

## Example entry

```markdown
## [2026-06-09 14:32] — tokenizer truncation support

**TL;DR:** Added max_tokens truncation to tokenize_corpus; e2e test passes. First
attempt using itertools.islice was discarded for a length check.

**Long description:** Training runs were exhausting memory on the full corpus.
Added a `max_tokens: int | None` parameter to `tokenize_corpus`
(src/data/tokenizer.py:41). Proved the approach first in
tests/test_tokenizer_truncation.py against a 3-document fixture, then integrated.
Ran `make test`: 14 passed in 2.31s.

**What worked:** Length check after each document append; truncation exact at
boundary. `pytest tests/e2e/test_pipeline.py -v` → 3 passed.

**What failed:** First tried `itertools.islice` over a generator — broke the
document-order guarantee callers rely on. Error from e2e test:
`AssertionError: token 4096 expected 17, got 102`.

**What was kept / discarded:** Kept length-check version and the new test.
Discarded islice version (never committed).

**Open questions / next steps:** `build_training_batches` still loads the full
token list into memory; streaming batches would remove the need for truncation
entirely. Deferred — out of scope for this task.
```
